co_narrows_the_2.blurb: The Narrows is a stretch of Poudre Canyon west of Fort Collins where big, steep walls rise right beside the road. Sport climbing makes up the largest share, with a good block of bouldering and a smaller amount of trad. Across the canyon the rock mixes granite, gneiss and schist, and quality swings from solid to loose, so a helmet is wise. Roped grades run from about 5.9 to 5.13, with most between 5.10 and 5.12; boulder problems span V0 to V11. Sheep Mountain is the biggest crag, mostly sport, with south-facing walls that suit winter days. Narrows Blocs, Widowmakers and the Twilight Area round out the larger zones.

nj_a_northwest.blurb: Northwest New Jersey, across Sussex and Warren counties, has the state's largest share of roped climbing along with plenty of bouldering. Along the Kittatinny Ridge, at High Point and the Delaware Water Gap, the rock is metaquartzite layered with shale, while Allamuchy State Park has crystalline granite. Trad is the main roped style, with a lot of top-roping and a good amount of bouldering; ice shows up in winter at the Water Gap. Roped grades are mostly 5.4 to 5.10, with a few harder lines, and boulders range from V0 to V7. Delaware Water Gap, Cranberry Hollow and Allamuchy State Park are the largest sub-areas. The scene is low-key and local, with few published details.

pa_northeast_ridges_and_valleys.blurb: This part of northeastern Pennsylvania spreads over ridges, valleys and plateaus, taking in the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos, with climbing near towns such as Allentown, Scranton and Stroudsburg. Bouldering is the biggest draw, followed by trad, with some sport, top-roping and winter ice. Boulders mostly sit between V0 and V5 and stretch up to V9; roped climbs run from about 5.5 to 5.12 and a few above. Mocanaqua has the most sport and boulders, including highballs, on quartzite in former coal country. Delaware Water Gap is the trad center, with multi-pitch climbing on Mount Minsi. Bauer Rock and Emmaus Boulders add more bouldering options.

ca_south_shore_2.blurb: South Shore covers the California side of Lake Tahoe, around the town of South Lake Tahoe and rising toward Echo Summit, at roughly 6,300 feet. Bouldering is the largest part, followed by sport, with some trad, top-roping and a few scrambles. Boulder problems run from V0 to V11 across a broad spread, while sport grades mostly sit between 5.9 and 5.12. The Pie Shop is the biggest area, a dome-like formation with coarse rock and a southern exposure that keeps it climbable in winter. Meyers Area adds more boulders, and Luther Spires and Luther Rock are the main sport and trad crags. Fixed hardware varies a lot in quality.

ca_highway_38_crags.blurb: The crags along Highway 38 are tucked into the San Bernardino Mountains, many inside small canyons beside Mill Creek. Sport climbing leads, with a solid bouldering scene and only a little trad. Frustration Creek is a slot canyon with steep granite sport in three tiers, from easy lower routes to an upper tier full of 5.13s. Monkeyface Falls is another canyon with waterfalls, climbs on both walls and plenty of tree shade, making it a favorite in summer; Thurman Flat adds sport and boulders close to the creek. Sport grades run from about 5.6 to 5.13, mostly 5.10 to 5.12, and the boulders skew easy. Climbing is possible through most of the year.

co_mt_evans.blurb: Mt. Blue Sky is a high alpine area on Colorado's Front Range, about 30 miles west of Denver, topping out at 14,153 feet. The rock is granite, with cliffs holding trad and alpine routes up to about 1,400 feet, plus some aid. Bouldering is the largest part, on rough, featured stone with incut edges. Roped grades run from about 5.7 to 5.13, and problems from V0 to V15 with most falling between V1 and V10. Lincoln Lake Slabs, the Black Wall and the Aprons are among the main roped zones. The season is short: the boulders sit above 10,000 feet, afternoon storms and snow are common, the air is thin and the walk-ins can be long.
